• DOE Launches Competition to Accelerate Development of World’s First Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computer
    September 17, 2026

    The U.S. Department of Energy has launched the Quantum Genesis Q Competition, with up to $215 million in planned funding to accelerate development of the world’s first fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computers. The competition challenges private-sector companies to demonstrate systems with at least 100 logical qubits and advance quantum computing toward tackling meaningful and difficult scientific problems. Complementing the competition, DOE’s Quantum High-Performance Computing Validation and Verification Testbed Lab Call will provide $45 million in planned funding to National Laboratories to develop the capabilities needed to rigorously characterize and validate quantum systems across the computing stack. Together, these efforts will help move quantum computing from technology demonstrations toward a powerful new tool for scientific discovery. They also advance the goals of the President’s Executive Order, Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation, including the Quantum Computer for Application Development and Discovery Science (QC-ADDS) Effort.

  • Eight NSF Quantum Leap Challenge Institutes announced
    August 26, 2026

    Understanding and wielding the quantum properties of nature is the ambitious objective of eight research institutes that will collectively receive more than $290 million from the U.S. National Science Foundation. The investment is an expansion of the NSF Quantum Leap Challenge Institutes program, which NSF created in 2020 as part of the agency’s strategy to fulfill the 2018 “National Quantum Initiative Act.”

    Categories: Centers, NSF
